summary.headline: HFCL Q2 FY27 consolidated PAT ₹394.22 crore (+448% YoY) on revenue ₹2,541.79 crore; order book ₹28,900 crore; management guides ≥80% FY27 revenue growth.
summary.overview: Management reported its best-ever quarter: consolidated revenue ₹2,541.79 crore (up ~143.6% YoY, +32.7% QoQ), EBITDA ₹658.00 crore (25.89% margin), and PAT ₹394.22 crore (15.51% margin). H1 FY27 PBT was ₹870.12 crore and PAT ₹639.86 crore. Guidance was raised from ~20% to ~40% and now to at least 80% revenue growth for FY27, with defence and connectivity solutions cited as new growth legs. Several answers were qualitative or deferred, notably on the defence ramp-up, EPC restructuring timing and FY28 guidance.

financial_highlights.change: +223.55% YoY; +47.78% QoQ; margin +640 bps YoY, +264 bps QoQ
as referenced by analyst; not restated by management

financial_highlights.value: Q1 FY27 nil; Q2 FY27 ~₹300 crore; FY27 target ~₹800 crore

segments.name: Optical fibre cable (OFC) / telecom & data centre
segments.commentary: Telecom segment revenue ~₹2,300 crore cited by analyst; management split ~70:30 hyperscalers vs conventional telcos and later 65–75% data centre vs 25–35% telecom by revenue. Fibre capacity runs at 100% in value terms; OFC capacity to rise from 39 to 63 million fibre km, fibre from 28 to 43 million km.

segments.name: Defence & Aerospace
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 defence revenue ~₹80 crore per analyst. FY27 aspiration ~₹500 crore (management also cited ₹500–600 crore), FY28 at least ₹2,000 crore, 3-year aspiration ₹5,000 crore. Aerospace acquisition expected to close in Q2 FY27 with unexecuted order book ~₹1,600 crore.

segments.name: EPC / O&M
segments.commentary: Segment loss of ~₹121 crore in Q2 FY27 attributed to BharatNet expenses booked before milestone bills were raised. Management expects losses of ₹75–100 crore over the next two quarters combined and profit from Q1 FY28. O&M order book ~₹5,000 crore; BSNL first-year AMC approval expected in ~1–2 weeks.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth of at least 80% YoY, up from initial ~20% and later ~40% aspiration.
Management expects Q3 FY27 revenue to grow QoQ from Q2 level; FY28 guidance not given, but said numbers should be better than current.
Connectivity solutions revenue target ~₹800 crore for FY27 and ~₹2,000 crore for FY28.
Defence revenue ~₹500 crore FY27, at least ₹2,000 crore FY28, ₹5,000 crore in ~3 years.
₹10,000 crore revenue milestone now expected well before FY29.
Margins expected to improve somewhat, aided by capacity, backward integration and connectivity mix; management said no reversal expected.
Own preform capacity doubling from 300 to 600 MT, commissioning October 2028; mid-term preform solution from calendar Q1 2027; debt expected to fall substantially in FY27–FY28.
capex_capacity: Planned investment ~₹1,800 crore across optical fibre, cable and preform manufacturing.
Fibre capacity 28 to 38 million km, then to 43 million km; cable capacity 39 to 56 million fibre km, then to 63 million fibre km.
Preform 600 MT (doubled from 300 MT) targeted for October 2028; own preform covers about half of the 45 million km capacity, rest bought externally under long-term contracts.
Ammunition manufacturing complex in Andhra Pradesh on 1,000 acres allotted by state government; revenue expected in about 2 years; hand grenade tender for 800,000 units submitted.
Board committee with E&Y advice reviewing EPC restructuring; recommendation expected within about 1–2 weeks, with Board decision in about 2 weeks.
demand_pricing: Order book ₹28,900 crore (vs ~₹26,000 crore prior quarter), with management stating ~₹2,500 crore delivered and ~₹5,500 crore new orders in the quarter. Analyst cited ~₹18,500 crore OFC and data centre interconnect book; management estimated ~70% of export orders from hyperscalers.
Management sees no slowdown from US rate concerns; expects demand pickup in Europe, Asia and telcos, and says telco orders are at concrete inquiry stage.
Fibre price rose sharply in Q2 (cited ~20%) and is now stabilising; preform prices in the open market cited as up ~600% and expected to fall, with HFCL on pre-fixed contracts.
Long-term contracts have annual or 18–24 month price-reset clauses; 4–6 month contracts have no reset clause.
Data centre fibre (A2, 180 micron) priced ~USD25–27/km vs telco G.657B ~USD15, per management.

qa_highlights.question: Share of hyperscalers in ₹18,500 crore OFC/DC book and customer concentration?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined customer names (NDA); estimated ~70% of export orders from hyperscalers, with domestic orders mostly from telcos. Data centres in India yet to pick up.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 guidance of 80%+ growth conservative, implying flat-to-lower H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said guidance is deliberately conservative; denied preform or supply constraints.

qa_highlights.question: Margin trajectory over next 2 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margins will improve somewhat, driven by high-capacity fibre demand, connectivity products, and preform backward integration from late 2028.

qa_highlights.question: Split of telecom revenue between conventional telcos and hyperscalers, and utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Approximately 70:30 hyperscalers to telcos. Fibre runs at 100% of capacity; cable utilisation varies by product, but 100% on a revenue-value basis.

qa_highlights.question: Defence revenue bridge from ~₹80 crore H1 to ₹500 crore FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Electro-optic sights already ramping; Foliage Penetration Radar nearing approval; aerospace acquisition with ~₹1,600–1,800 crore order book to contribute from this quarter.

qa_highlights.question: When will the EPC segment turn profitable?
qa_highlights.answer: Q2 loss of ~₹121 crore due to unbilled BharatNet work; next two quarters combined loss ₹75–100 crore; profit expected from Q1 FY28. BSNL AMC approval pending.

qa_highlights.question: Did pricing or volume drive QoQ growth? Connectivity revenue in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said both; declined to split. Connectivity revenue ~₹300 crore in Q2 and ~₹800 crore targeted for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Germanium supply and FY28 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Germanium needed in ~2 years; talks with suppliers underway. No FY28 numerical guidance given.

risks_watch: Preform and germanium supply: preform open-market prices cited as elevated; germanium needed in ~2 years and supply contracts not yet finalised.
Defence ramp-up gap: ₹80 crore H1 versus ₹500 crore FY27 aspiration needs a steep H2 step-up; aerospace acquisition closing expected this quarter.
EPC segment losses and pending restructuring decision; BSNL AMC approval and BharatNet bill realisation timing.
Customer concentration with hyperscalers; data centre demand sensitivity to financing costs (raised by analyst, management dismissed as a material risk).
Capacity additions (fibre and preform) could pressure pricing as supply grows; management expects preform prices to fall.
Limited disclosure: customer-level data under NDA, no FY28 guidance, and a stated uncertainty on the H1 revenue split.
summary.management_tone: Highly confident and expansive on growth, margins and defence, with repeated optimism about the order book and pipeline. Evasive or deflecting on specifics: declined to split price vs volume, avoided FY28 guidance, and did not quantify the USD1.1 billion hyperscaler order revenue or utilisation by product.
key_quotes: It is my privilege to present the best ever quarterly performance in HFCL's history that marks a defining moment in our growth journey.
we expect revenue growth of at least 80% in this financial year.
Friends, I want to emphasise that we do not see this quarter as a peak, but as the sustained phase of strong growth.
There is no chance I see of getting reverse or less.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of at least 80% (raised from ~20%, then ~40%), backed by a ₹28,900 crore order book, fibre running at 100% with capacity rising to 63 million fibre km, and ~₹1,800 crore planned capex, though most capacity additions are only 2+ quarters away and defence/EPC timing remains qualitative.
